Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.
Comments: Business-to-business (B2B) electronic transfers are supported through bank payment rails/RTGS; BCT payment bulletin evidence indicates strong usage of electronic transfers (virements) in clearing/settlement volumes, consistent with B2B payment capability.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with fresher, more specific sources: business-facing mobile wallet products (STB Pay Pro Entreprise; IZI Pay for merchants/entrepreneurs, 2025) allow real-time transfers to and from business accounts and merchant collections via Tunisia's mobile payment (TUNPAY/SMT) rails, corroborating the original BCT bulletin's bank-transfer data. Value Code 2 (Yes) confirmed, not changed.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border interoperability is developing: Tunisia (via BCT) joined PAPSS (Pan-African Payment and Settlement System) in Feb 2024, enabling regional cross-border payments integration though not necessarily fully mature end-to-end consumer interoperability.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: PAPSS's own June 2026 network-coverage document lists Tunisia as 'LIVE SOON' with no live commercial bank participants; a February 2025 report confirms Tunisian banks were still being urged to onboard over a year after BCT's central-bank-level membership (Feb 2024). Actual cross-border functionality therefore remains under development rather than partially functional; downgraded from 4 to 3.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Evidence of consumer protection specific to digital payments was limited; available sources emphasize BCT-led digital transformation/financial inclusion and general protections in wallet offerings, but no clear, dedicated payment consumer-protection statute or enforceable scheme-level consumer recourse framework was identified in the reviewed materials.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original LinkedIn source was inaccessible (paywalled) and non-authoritative. Loi n°2005-51 (27 June 2005) on electronic fund transfers imposes dedicated payment consumer-protection obligations (pre-contract disclosure of fees and dispute terms, free contractual-conditions document, loss/unauthorised-use notification procedures), and BCT Circular 2018-16 explicitly requires payment institutions to operate a 'dispositif de protection du consommateur'. This is dedicated payment-specific legislation, not merely general consumer law; upgraded from 2 (Partial) to 3 (Yes).

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: Government adoption of digital payment rails is evidenced but appears limited in scale/quantification: the BCT/IFC Paysmart platform was launched to ease bill payments (public/utility bills), indicating government-supported adoption but without clear coverage metrics or broad G2P digitization evidence.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: World Bank reporting indicates 44.4% of AMEN social-assistance cash transfers are digitalised (undated, c.2023-24), consistent with the existing 20-49% band, but this covers only one social-assistance programme, not the full G2P basket (salaries, pensions, all transfers) the variable requires; the original Paysmart source concerns bill payments, not G2P. No consolidated cross-programme G2P digitisation figure for Tunisia was found (Global Findex country-level breakdown could not be retrieved). Value Code 2 retained as the best available estimate but flagged for human review pending a comprehensive G2P figure.
